chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Organ pedals and bass technique
summary: He explains foot manuals, the hand bass extension and heel-and-toe, and Virgil Fox.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: What about... It's the small pedal, I think you said...

Well, actually... You can play that. But then there's another extension on the hand manual of the bass. So actually you're not playing with your foot all the time. You're playing the bass with your hand. But it gives it the illusion you're playing with your feet.
I see. Because I always wondered how hard that was to learn, to play with the feet.

Well, yeah. Well, they don't play with their feet. They just use strategic notes, you know, where they can rest on the pedal. You know, some do; organists like David Selby. You know, he's not a Jazz player, but he's a regular organist, and he uses the heel-and-toe method.
Well, did you use your feet on the pedal?
Oh, I like to use my feet on the pedal. You know, on a fast number, it's impossible to have an even bass line with your feet alone. I mean, at certain tempos, it's
Ramirez - 127
practically impossible.
You've got your small finger(?)... I used to look at that, and it seemed to be so easy to...
Well, it is easy according to what you're playing.
No, but it would be so easy to hit a wrong one!
Well, it's like anything, you know. You practice and...
Well, you know, it's easier if you're talented. But I never thought that would... They're pretty close together. What do you call those things down there?
Well, you manage to... You alternate the heel and toe. It all depends on what you're playing.
But what do you call those things down there for your feet? Are those pedals.
Yeah. They're foot manuals.
Foot manuals.
Foot keyboard. I don't know the terminology. I mean, you have various ways to describe it. Actually, it's nothing but a keyboard really...
Yes, for the feet.
Yes.
But instead of ten fingers, you've only got two.
Exactly. An illustration of that should be
Ramirez - 128

...(?)... The highest element... I mean, the most predominant artist in that respect would have been the late Virgil Fox, who received...who played these Classical numbers, and you'd see his feet going like hands. That's something to see. To show you how you can develop that technique, to what extent; you know, how to get there. But in Jazz you just cannot keep that rhythm going that way with your feet. Well, I mean, it can be mastered as much as you have... If you can help it with your hands, you have much better control.
